::: {#exm-cubic-big-o}
#### Finding witnesses for $2 n^3 + 40 = O(n^3)$

To prove $2 n^3 + 40 = O(n^3)$ (@def-big-o), we look for witnesses (@def-witness) $c$ and $N$.
Since $2 n^3 + 40 > 2 n^3$, the term $2 n^3$ needs $c > 2$.
With $c = 3$, the inequality $2 n^3 + 40 \le 3 n^3$ is the same as $40 \le n^3$,
which holds when $n \ge 4$, since $4^3 = 64$, but not when $n = 3$, since $3^3 = 27$.
So for every natural number $n \ge 4$,

$$
\ba
\abs{2 n^3 + 40}
&= 2 n^3 + 40
&& \text{(} 2 n^3 + 40 > 0 \text{)}
\\&\le 2 n^3 + n^3
&& \text{(} 40 \le 64 \le n^3 \text{, since } n \ge 4 \text{)}
\\&= 3 \abs{n^3},
\ea
$$

and $c = 3$, $N = 4$ are witnesses.
A larger $c$ allows a smaller $N$:
since $40 \le 40 n^3$ for every $n \ge 1$, the pair $c = 42$, $N = 1$ also works.

:::
